raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Refs #38587 (the SGLang-side half; the nested reproduction in that issue is decided by xgrammar's JSON-schema converter and was handled upstream).

For a strict Kimi-K3 tool, `_strict_arguments_format` emits the declared properties as fixed slots and then appends the `additionalProperties` branch as a `StarFormat` whose key matcher is `[^"& \t\r\n\f\v=<>]+`, i.e. any key. So a declared name can reappear under the looser additional schema: with

```json
{"properties": {"label": {"type": "string", "pattern": "[a-z]+"}, "score": {"type": "integer"}},
 "required": ["label"], "additionalProperties": {"type": "string"}}
```

the grammar accepts `score` as a `string` argument, and with the default `additionalProperties: true` it accepts `label` a second time with any type. JSON Schema applies `additionalProperties` only to keys that `properties` does not name, so the strict guarantee for declared keys was only as strong as the additional schema.

## Modifications

- `kimik3_structural_tag.py`: the additional-argument key regex now excludes the declared property names. xgrammar's regex dialect has no lookahead, so `_dynamic_key_pattern` builds the exclusion from a trie of the names: a key is acceptable when it leaves the trie with a character no declared name continues with, or when it stops at a proper prefix of one (`data_x`, `datab`, `databases` stay valid next to a declared `data` / `database`). Keys that cannot appear in XTML (containing `"`, `&`, whitespace, `=`, `<`, `>`) are skipped. Non-strict tools keep the unrestricted matcher.
- Two regression tests in `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_kimik3_structural_tag.py`: declared keys keep their own schema under both `additionalProperties: true` and a schema-valued one (undeclared keys still follow the additional schema), and only exact declared names are excluded.

## Accuracy Tests

No model code changes. On `main` the new cases fail (`assert not True` on the `score`-as-string and repeated-`label` calls); with the fix the whole `test_kimik3_structural_tag.py` passes (38 tests) and `test_function_call_parser.py` passes. CPU only, Python 3.12.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the key regex gains one alternative per trie node of the declared names, compiled once per tool set like the rest of the structural tag.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -347,15 +347,74 @@ def _known_argument_format(
     return OrFormat(elements=variants)
 
 
+# Regex text of the characters an argument key may not contain, and the same
+# characters as a Python set.
+_KEY_FORBIDDEN_CHARS = r'"& \t\r\n\f\v=<>'
+_KEY_FORBIDDEN_SET = set('"& \t\r\n\f\v=<>')
+
+
+def _regex_literal(text: str) -> str:
+    """Escape ``text`` for xgrammar's regex dialect, inside or outside a class."""
+    return "".join(
+        char
+        if char.isascii() and (char.isalnum() or char == "_")
+        else f"\\{char}"
+        if char.isascii()
+        else f"\\u{ord(char):04x}"
+        if ord(char) <= 0xFFFF
+        else f"\\U{ord(char):08x}"
+        for char in text
+    )
+
+
+def _dynamic_key_pattern(excluded_keys: Iterable[str]) -> str:
+    """Regex for an argument key that is none of ``excluded_keys``.
+
+    A strict tool pins each declared property to its own schema, so the
+    additionalProperties branch must not accept a declared name under the
+    looser schema (JSON Schema applies additionalProperties only to keys that
+    ``properties`` does not name). xgrammar's regex dialect has no lookahead,
+    so the exclusion walks a trie of the names: a key is acceptable when it
+    leaves the trie with a character no excluded name continues with, or when
+    it stops at a proper prefix of an excluded name.
+    """
+    any_key_char = f"[^{_KEY_FORBIDDEN_CHARS}]"
+    names = {key for key in excluded_keys if key and not set(key) & _KEY_FORBIDDEN_SET}
+    if not names:
+        return any_key_char + "+"
+
+    trie: Dict[str, Any] = {}
+    for name in names:
+        node = trie
+        for char in name:
+            node = node.setdefault(char, {})
+        node[""] = {}
+
+    alternatives: List[str] = []
+
+    def walk(node: Dict[str, Any], prefix: str) -> None:
+        children = [char for char in node if char]
+        diverge = f"[^{_KEY_FORBIDDEN_CHARS}{''.join(map(_regex_literal, children))}]"
+        alternatives.append(f"{_regex_literal(prefix)}{diverge}{any_key_char}*")
+        if prefix and "" not in node:
+            alternatives.append(_regex_literal(prefix))
+        for char in children:
+            walk(node[char], prefix + char)
+
+    walk(trie, "")
+    return "(?:" + "|".join(alternatives) + ")"
+
+
 def _dynamic_argument_format(

     root_schema: Dict[str, Any],
     loose_strings: bool = False,

-                RegexFormat(pattern=r'[^"& \t\r\n\f\v=<>]+'),
